 Coach Jesse Minter 's Baltimore Ravens welcomed the winless Los Angeles Chargers to M&T Bank Stadium and fell behind 10-0 in the first quarter following an impressive Justin Herbert touchdown run . Ravens offensive coordinator Declan Doyle gave a vote of confidence to starting QB Jacoby Brissett , but it was tough sledding against Chris O'Leary's defense in the early going.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Brissett limped to the sideline after rookie guard Olaivavega Ioane was driven into him. The pocket collapsed as Brissett went down with Chargers linebacker Tuli Tuipulotu on top of him.
 Brissett stayed in the game as Ravens fans became upset with the team's blocking on social media. The former Arizona Cardinals starting quarterback's offense finished with just 40 yards in the first quarter, including 39 passing yards and a single rushing yard. Mark Andrews, Justice Hill, and Derrick Henry all caught passes for coach Minter's team, but Henry did not record a yard on two carries.
 Former Ravens star Shannon Sharpe chimed in during the game, expressing worry over his former team's offense. The 0-8 Chargers had 128 total yards after one quarter, including over 50 yards rushing and 50 yards passing, suggesting Sharpe should probably the worry about the defense as well.
 Click Above to Subscribe Brissett is a newcomer to the Ravens' organization who was thrust into a difficult situation. He's known for his ability to adjust to any team, and to take care of the football using short passes, but he wasn't able to get much going in the first quarter.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The Ravens looked in serious danger of falling to 4-6 as the game continued on, with Minter's team in need of a spark.
